{{RequisiteWeapon|Ingredient For = {{Weapon|Mutalist Cernos}}}} {{Top|Lotus|Tenno|Tenno|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|Evoking the design of ancient bows, the high impact Cernos is perfect for hunting down highly shielded enemies.}} The '''Cernos''' is a {{Faction|Tenno}} Bow, and the first one available to new players that deals mainly {{D|Impact}} damage over another type. This weapon can be sold for {{cc|10,500}}. It is also a [[weapon crafting ingredient]] for {{Weapon|Mutalist Cernos}}. {{Checklist|nocategory=true| * {{Weapon|Cernos}} → {{Weapon|Mutalist Cernos}} * {{Weapon|Mutalist Cernos}} → {{Weapon|Proboscis Cernos}} (extra Cernos is needed if player wants to keep one copy of Mutalist Cernos) }} ==Characteristics== This weapon deals primarily {{D|Impact}} damage. {{Advantages|class=Bow|}} {{Disadvantages|class=Bow|}} {{WeaponComparison|Cernos Prime}} {{WeaponComparison|Rakta Cernos|header=n}} ==Acquisition== The Cernos's blueprint can be purchased from the [[Market]]. {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} ==Tips== *Despite what its description says, the Cernos is most effective against {{Faction|Grineer}} , which are primarily ''armored,'' not shielded. Its damage spread being weighted primarily towards Impact means the majority of the weapon's damage will inherit the element's [[Faction Damage Bonus]] against them, dealing solid damage even through their armor. **Impact's status effect of reducing the target's [[Mercy]] threshold also logically counteracts their armor, allowing heavy enemies to be executed even with most of their health remaining, once their [[Overguard]] is broken, after suffering enough Impact procs. ***While the Cernos has a low base status chance relative to its rate of fire and projectile count, this can easily be fixed with modding. {{M|Rifle Aptitude}} will bring it up to a respectable 34%, which can be rolled multiple times per shot by adding multishot mods, such as {{M|Split Chamber}}. **Adding Corrosive damage to the Cernos is a good idea, enhancing how much damage it can do to Grineer enemies even further. **The Cernos is also strong against enemies of the {{Faction|Scaldra}} and {{Faction|Anarchs}} factions, though by the time the player is able to fight these enemies, they will likely have replaced the Cernos with a superior weapon, such as one of its upgraded counterparts. *The Cernos is very statistically similar to the {{Weapon|Paris}} and {{Weapon|Dread}}, two other Bows that become available by the time it is. The three primarily vary in which physical element they are most weighted towards, though the Dread will generally be the last of the three a new player obtains unless they're especially lucky. Thus, if the player has used either of the other two Bows, they will likely know how to use the Cernos. *With a maxed {{M|Critical Delay}} mod, the Cernos' [[critical chance]] will increase to 103.3%. This breaks the 100% critical chance threshold, guaranteeing every hit will be a critical hit and giving the weapon a very small chance to "orange crit", whereupon a critical hit will have its critical multiplier doubled. **Using a maxed Critical Delay however will also drastically reduce the Cernos's [[fire rate]], due to mods that modify this stat having their effect doubled on Bows, making each Cernos arrow take a long time to draw back. This can be countered with the usage of a fire rate mod, such as {{M|Speed Trigger}}. ***Even with only {{M|Point Strike}}, the Cernos will reach 90% critical chance, causing its hits to be critical far more often than they aren't. **If this modding avenue is chosen, adding as many critical damage mods to the Cernos as possible is advised, as they will apply on every hit for a very large damage increase. **At the Mastery Rank the Cernos is unlocked, the Dread and {{Weapon|Cinta}} are also capable of exceeding 100% critical chance. Of the three, the Cernos is generally the easiest to obtain. ==Trivia== *The name "Cernos" means "horn" in Gaulish. *Despite being more effective against the highly-armored {{Faction|Grineer}}, the Cernos's description says it's effective against "highly shielded enemies", implying it's effective against the Corpus instead, who are instead vulnerable to {{D|Puncture}} damage. This is an artifact from before [[Update 36|Update 36.0]], where [[Damage 2.0|Damage 2.0's]] health types system instead made Impact damage stronger against [[Shield|energy shielding]] regardless of faction, while Puncture was stronger against most forms of armor. After the update, which replaced this system with [[Damage 3.0|Damage 3.0's]] faction multipliers and swapped the Corpus and Grineer's vulnerabilities, the Cernos's description was not updated to compensate, and still has not been as of [[Update 41: The Old Peace#Hotfix 41.1.2|Hotfix 41.1.2]] (2-17-2026). *Being an Impact oriented bow, the Cernos uses arrows with a mace-like head, with a larger impact area. This spreads the kinetic energy of the arrows across a wider area, creating a blunt impact, hence its damage distribution. **Despite this, the Cernos's arrows can still pin enemies they kill to walls. Judging by the hole in the middle of the head, it's possible the arrows are hollow to house a spring-loaded punch system that fires a spike upon impact, though no such animation exists in-game if [[Captura]] mode's camera is used to watch the arrows mid-flight. **The [[Prisma Arrows|Prisma Arrows skin]] highly resembles the Cernos's arrows, and can be equipped to any Bow-type weapon. *As of {{ver|30.3}}, the Cernos has the most variations of all weapons, having a total of 5 weapons in its family; the normal {{Weapon|Cernos}}, {{Weapon|Rakta Cernos}}, {{Weapon|Cernos Prime}}, {{Weapon|Mutalist Cernos}}, and {{Weapon|Proboscis Cernos}}. **The Cernos is the first weapon to have two upgraded forms, with both its Mutalist and Proboscics variants requiring the other form respectively in order to be built. **The Cernos is also one of the few weapons to have variants that are considered separate weapons for the sake of mechanics like Riven mods, rather than direct variants, that aren't simply an akimbo version of the weapon. The {{Weapon|Quanta}} is another. ==Media== Warframe0150.jpg|Cernos in the Codex. {{Top|Lotus|Tenno|Tenno|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{codex|The remotely triggered Castanas quietly deliver a lethal dose of electricity to unsuspecting enemies.}} The '''Castanas''' are {{Faction|Tenno}} throwing type secondary weapons with {{D|Electricity}} detonation charge that can be detonated remotely by using the [[Alternate Fire]], much like the {{Weapon|Penta}}. Although lacking in throwing speed like other thrown weapons, they can be stacked up to six then detonated all at once to create a wide array of crowd controlling opportunities, thanks to their electrical explosion and chaining effects. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals {{D|Electricity}} damage. **Guaranteed {{D|Electricity}} proc. *Mines can stick to surfaces, including enemies and allies. **Extra projectiles generated by [[Multishot]] have a very wide horizontal spread, effective at covering large groups of enemies. **Can only have six deployed mines out at once. ***Extra projectiles generated by [[Multishot]] will count towards this limit. *User can detonate charges on command via [[Alternate Fire]], giving the player precise timing in detonation. **Detonation has an explosion radius of '''3.6''' meters. **Up to six deployed mines can be ready for simultaneous detonation. **Explosion does not need direct line of sight to deal damage and will penetrate walls. **Explosions inflict [[Stagger|self-stagger]]. **Explosion has linear damage falloff from 100% to 60% from central impact. **Can benefit from {{M|Fulmination}} ({{M|Primed Fulmination|Primed}}). *Innate two {{Pol|Madurai}} polarities. {{Advantages| *Pinpoint [[accuracy]]. *[[Silent]], even if the projectile hits the enemy. }} {{Disadvantages| *Projectiles have very slow travel time with arcing. *Semi-automatic fire, unlike other throwing weapons. *Extremely low magazine size of just 2 rounds; requires frequent reloading. }} {{WeaponComparison|Sancti Castanas}} ==Acquisition== The Castana's blueprint can be [[research]]ed from the [[Research/Tenno Lab|Tenno Lab]] in the [[dojo]]. {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} This weapon can be sold for 5,000 credits ==Notes== *The normal animation and arc behaves similar to other thrown secondary weapons. *Castanas can stun-lock bosses such as Lech Kril. *Primary fire throws the Castanas, secondary fire detonates them. *Charges will stick to any surface (enemies, allies, [[companion]]s, etc.); after sticking, they will proc {{D|Electricity}} with 100% chance when detonated. **When thrown while running backwards, it is possible that they can stick to your Sentinel or your Frame itself. **This guaranteed {{D|Electricity}} proc does not damage the user even if when dealing self-damage. *Throws that were made by the left hand are further from reticle by a few degrees to the bottom compared to the right hand. *Can not proc {{D|Radiation}} on user. *When {{M|Magnum Force}} is added, the Castanas will begin to spread apart on throws if [[Multishot]] mods are applied. This may be helpful for combating the small blast radius they have by spacing them slightly apart from each other. *The Castanas are currently subject to a bug that dramatically increases projectile spread when using [[multishot]] mods. Equipping a low-rank {{M|Magnum Force}} will fix this. *Throwing these at an Arctic Eximus snowglobe and detonating them will kill the Eximus. *Castanas thrown by {{WF|Mirage}}'s illusions from {{A|Hall of Mirrors}} will not interfere with the maximum amount of armed Castanas at a given time. ==Tips== *Mirage's Hall of Mirrors can be used to increase the number of Castanas that can be planted, but the holograms' Castanas will detonate a few seconds after impact; though they will not damage the player and can still also be detonated manually in the given time they are active. ==Trivia== *The Castanas are the first thrown secondary weapon that delivers Area of Effect damage. *The detonation feature is similar to that of the {{Weapon|Penta}} grenade launcher, which also allowed users to detonate on command. *The word ''Castañas'' means "chestnuts" in Spanish and Greek, judging how the knives are thrown, then "open" themselves, revealing their explosive cores. *The Castanas are the first throwable weapon of its kind to be thrown in "Semi-auto". ==Bugs== *If Multishot is modded onto the Castanas in any way and happens to activate, the castanas thrown will travel in widely different directions, landing far away from the intended target. **This can be counteracted with {{M|Magnum Force}}. ==Media== Castanaspic.png|Castanas In The Market Castanas-Website.jpg|Castanas in Website {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|7SbkkoQabTc|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|iLvkvaerr3U|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|6zY3TOlnq7k|size=300px}} }} {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|32.2}} *Fixed the Critical Chance and Status Chance stats not being listed for the Castanas in the Arsenal. {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''Secondary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 4 Ammo per Pick Up: *Castanas ;GENERAL CHANGES: *Updated thrown weapons to now only show a single projectile in hand when only one 1 projectile is remaining before reloading. This affects the following weapons: **Castanas {{ver|27.2.2}}
Reduced the following AoE weapons Radial Damage Falloff from central impact that were all previously 90%: *Castanas: 40% {{ver|27.2}} ;Self Damage Changes: We are getting rid of Self Damage and replacing it with something else: instead of Self Damage, it’s now ‘Stagger’. This change completely removes the chance of killing yourself, and instead now creates scenarios where you will interrupt yourself - or ‘Stagger’ - to varying degrees if you aren’t careful. The degrees of Self-Interrupt start with a small stumble all the way to full knockdown depending on how close you are to the center of explosion. Any Mods referring to Self Damage will be converted to acknowledge Stagger. With this Self-Interrupt system, we have added dozens of new recovery animations that harness a ninja-like recovery experience. By pressing ‘Jump’ at the correct time, you can execute a ninja-skill-based knockdown recovery to ALL in-game knockdowns. This ninja recovery window is indicated by a glowing FX on your Warframe. In the original Dev Workshop, we said:
''As a result of this overall systemic change, Weapons with Stagger will be getting approximately a 20% buff in Damage, with any weapons with AOE receiving a 50% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact.'' This is no longer accurate after continued testing. What we are doing now is: No damage buffs have been added, but any weapons with AOE are receiving ~20% increase in Radius. Additionally, AOE weapons are receiving a 90% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact. This means on the very outer section of the explosion Radius 10% of the Damage will be dealt. Tactics will be deadly - aim true, Tenno. ''Why: Several players brought up the history of the Tonkor and we want to make sure we ship this change in a place that’s conservative in its starting point from a balance perspective. {{Top|Orokin|Orokin|Orokin|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons|Prime|Prime|Prime|}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|A noble bow to hunt hellish beasts.}} The '''Cernos Prime''' is the [[Prime]] variant of the {{Weapon|Cernos}}. Aside from increased damage, the Cernos Prime is unique in that it fires three arrows per shot in a horizontal spread, and has an [[Alternate Fire]] mode that shoots vertically, and deals bonus damage on [[Enemy Body Parts|headshots]]. It was released alongside {{WF|Valkyr Prime}} and {{Weapon|Venka Prime}}. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals primarily {{D|Impact}} damage. *Deals '''50%''' bonus damage on [[Enemy Body Parts|headshots]]. *Charged shots have innate 1 meter [[punch through]]. *Innate [[multishot]] of 3 arrows. **[[Alternate Fire]] can toggle a horizontal or vertical spread shot. *On kill, bodies will follow the arrow that killed them, damaging enemies in their path and pinning the corpse to walls. *Can use the bow-exclusive {{M|Thunderbolt}} mod. *[[Fire rate]] mods apply double their bonuses. *Innate two {{Pol|Madurai}} polarities. {{Advantages|class=Bow| *Fourth highest base damage of all bows, behind {{Weapon|Daikyu}} , {{Weapon|Lenz}} and {{Weapon|Kuva Bramma}}. *Pinpoint accuracy when aiming ({{Keybind|RMB}}). *[[Silent]]. }} {{Disadvantages|class=Bow| *Very wide spread. }} {{WeaponComparison|Cernos}} {{WeaponComparison|Rakta Cernos|header=n}} ==Acquisition== Unlike most Prime gear, Cernos Prime is permanently unvaulted, with relics being obtainable through [[Abandoned Derelict Caches]] in Corpus [[Railjack]] missions. {{PrimeTable}} {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} ===Vaulted=== *On [https://forums.warframe.com/topic/1007828-limbo-prime-access-ending-soon-valkyr-prime-entering-the-vault/ September 11th, 2018], it was announced that Cernos Prime, along with {{WF|Valkyr Prime}} and {{Weapon|Venka Prime}}, would enter the [[Prime Vault]] and be retired from the reward tables on September 25th, 2018. Any preexisting components or fully-built weapons will remain as is. *Cernos Prime, {{WF|Valkyr Prime}}, and {{Weapon|Venka Prime}} can occasionally be acquired via [[Prime Resurgence]], in addition to having their relics obtainable as part of the aforementioned [[Railjack]] missions. ==Notes== *The +50% bonus damage on [[Enemy Body Parts|headshots]] is multiplicative to other sources of +bonus damage on headshot such as {{Arcane|Primary Deadhead}} and {{A|Prowl}}. *The Cernos Prime's shots fire multiple arrows in a fanning spread. The number of arrows is affected by [[multishot]] mods, similar to shotguns. *[[Alternate Fire]] toggles a Horizontal Spread or Vertical Spread fire. *{{M|Heavy Caliber}} will decrease accuracy by a small amount, making each arrow fire slightly off from its normal trajectory. **As of {{ver|19.11.2}} this was increased dramatically, making the weapon act more like a wildly-spreading shotgun than a fan of arrows. **The arrows seem to be spread in a formation where some arrows are lower than the others, rather than being wider spread than others, this might make it difficult to get headshots with multiple arrows. * Low accuracy will effectively invert Cernos Prime's firing mode. Horizontal shots will follow generally vertical line of shot and vice versa. This behavior is best observed while using [[Split Flights]] ==Trivia== *The Cernos Prime, alongside {{Weapon|Afuris Prime}}, {{Weapon|Akbolto Prime}}, {{Weapon|Aksomati Prime}}, {{Weapon|Akstiletto Prime}}, {{Weapon|Ballistica Prime}}, {{Weapon|Dual Kamas Prime}}, {{Weapon|Dual Keres Prime}}, {{Weapon|Fang Prime}}, {{Weapon|Gunsen Prime}}, {{Weapon|Paris Prime}} and {{Weapon|Zhuge Prime}} are the only Prime weapons that do not require [[Orokin Cell]]s as crafting ingredients. ==Media== TriBowCodex.png|Cernos Prime in Codex. Cernos Prime Arsenal.png|Cernos Prime as shown in the Arsenal Cernos Prime Arsenal 2.png Cernos Prime Arrow quiver.png|Cernos Prime Arrow Quiver with Arrows {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|wn1wlYu4yUk|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|HCJ8hrCTUWE|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|7YPJ1kUyWIs|size=300px}} }} {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 15 Ammo per Pick Up: *Cernos Prime {{ver|30.9}} *Fixed the Cernos Prime Vertical Spread shot doing 2x damage of Horizontal Spread shot. {{ver|28}} *Reduced the hit FX of the Cernos Prime. {{ver|27.2.1}} *Increased Cernos Prime 10% Status Chance per projectile to 30% Status Chance per projectile. {{ver|27.2}} ;Greater than 100% Status having meaning: Shotguns have a unique Role here based on a very patch-work history with how they interact with Status Chance. A Shotgun that shoots 99% Status Chance would give you 35% (roughly) status per pellet. 100% Status Gives you 100% Status per pellet. This huge jump in performance happens with just a 1% gain - why? Well, to answer that we have to look at our choice to make what the UI conveys reality. It would feel broken to shoot a Shotgun with 100% Status and not see a perfect spread of Effects. In reality, to make Status consistent we have to treat Shotguns as a special case. Shotguns as a special case means we have buffed the Status Chance of all Shotguns by x3 or greater. The UI now behaves to show the reality that you are determining Status Chance per pellet. {{ver|25.7}} *Normalized quick shots to have the same critical chance/damage and status chance as charged shots. *While reviewing Bow stats the team has also refreshed all their FX (including the Lenz)! '''Cedo Prime''' is the [[Prime]]d counterpart of the {{Weapon|Cedo}} alchemical shotgun, acting as a direct upgrade. Cedo Prime was released alongside {{WF|Lavos Prime}} and {{Weapon|Dual Zoren Prime}}.

==Characteristics==
*This weapon deals primarily {{D|Puncture}} damage.
*Deals '''+60%''' bonus damage per unique status effect on target.
** On the Primary Fire, this bonus is '''additive''' to all base damage bonuses, such as [[Point Blank]] and [[Galvanized Savvy]].
** On '''direct hits''' from the Alternate Fire glaive, this bonus is additive with [[Galvanized Savvy]], and '''multiplicative''' to normal base damage bonuses like [[Point Blank]]. See [[Condition Overload (Mechanic)]] for more info.
** On '''explosions''' from the Alternate Fire glaive, this bonus does '''not''' apply.
*Primary Fire shoots wide-spread, close-ranged buckshot in a fully automatic fashion.
**Innate 0.8 meter [[punch through]].
**Innate [[multishot]] of 7 pellets.
*[[Alternate Fire]] launches a glaive that explodes in a '''6''' meter radius on impact with a surface or enemy and bounces up to '''11''' times.
**Direct hit and explosion apply status separately.
*** Direct hit deals {{D|Slash}} damage and has the listed status chance of '''50%''', affected by status chance bonuses and modded elements.
*** Explosion deals {{D|Blast}} damage and applies two separate '''guaranteed''' procs. The number of procs '''cannot''' be increased with status chance bonuses.
**** The first proc can be any element modded onto the weapon, or the innate {{D|Blast}} damage. The chance for each element follows normal status weighting rules.
**** The second proc has an even chance to be any of the following; {{D|Heat}}, {{D|Cold}}, {{D|Electricity}}, or {{D|Toxin}}.
**Explosion does not need direct line of sight to deal damage and will penetrate walls.
**Consumes no ammo.
**[[Multishot]] affects the number of glaives released per use, each with their own trajectory.
*Innate {{M|Shotgun Ammo Mutation}} effect when used by Lavos.
*Innate two {{Pol|Madurai}} and one {{Pol|Vazarin}} polarities.
